name: Sketch recognizable faces
blurb: Portraits are proportion before talent. The Loomis method gives you a reliable construction for the skull and features, and likeness follows from measurement rather than instinct.
gear: A pencil (HB and 2B), paper and a kneadable eraser
steps: Learn the proportions: eyes sit halfway down the head, the bottom of the nose halfway between eyes and chin, the mouth a third of the way from nose to chin.
Learn a construction method — the Loomis head — to place the skull, jaw and centre line before any feature goes in.
Draw each feature separately for a week: 50 eyes, 50 noses, 50 mouths, from reference.
Learn to see negative shapes and measure with your pencil at arm’s length, comparing widths to heights.
Learn basic shading: one light source, then block in the five values from core shadow to highlight.
Draw the same face from a photo, then flip your drawing horizontally to expose distortions you have gone blind to.
tips: Drawing features too high on the head is the universal beginner error. The eyes really are halfway down.
Draw what you see, not what you know. The symbol of an eye in your head is not shaped like an actual eye.
Flipping the image is the cheapest way to see your own mistakes.
proof: You draw a portrait from a photo that someone else recognises without being told who it is.
